title: Union, Intersection & Narrowing
subtitle: Advanced union types, type narrowing with typeof / instanceof / in, exhaustive checks
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: When you have a union type (string | number), TypeScript knows the value is one of those types but not which one. Using string methods on a number (or vice versa) would be an error — but TypeScript can't automatically know which branch you're in.
whyItExists.solution: Type narrowing: checks like typeof, instanceof, or in narrow the type within a branch. TypeScript's control flow analysis tracks which type is active in each block — after an if (typeof x === 'string') check, TypeScript treats x as string in that block.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Whenever you have a union type and need to access type-specific properties or methods. Also use discriminated union narrowing (switching on a kind field) for object unions.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Don't reach for as Type casts to avoid narrowing — that bypasses type checking. Write the proper guard instead.

explainModes.beginner: When a value can be a string OR a number, TypeScript doesn't know which one you have at a given point in the code. You need to check first ('if this is a string, do X; if it's a number, do Y'). TypeScript watches these checks and knows the type in each branch.
explainModes.simple: typeof x === 'string' narrows x to string. instanceof x narrows to a class type. 'prop' in x checks if x has that property. Discriminated union: switch on shape.kind narrows to specific variant. Exhaustive check: default: const _: never = x — TypeScript errors if x still has types left.
explainModes.standard: Control flow analysis: TypeScript tracks which types are possible at each code location after assignments, returns, throws, and type guards. Truthy/falsy narrowing: if (x) — narrows out null, undefined, 0, '' from the type. Equality narrowing: if (x === 'left') narrows x to 'left' (literal). Array.isArray() narrows to any[]. Type predicates (user-defined guards): function isString(x: unknown): x is string.
explainModes.technical: In expressions: 'length' in x — narrows x to types that have a length property. Negation: if (!cond) — narrows in the else branch. Optional chaining doesn't narrow: x?.prop doesn't narrow x to defined in the call. Assertion functions: function assertString(x: unknown): asserts x is string — after call, TS treats x as string (throws if not). Discriminant analysis: TypeScript analyzes which variants of a discriminated union can match each case.
explainModes.deepDive: TypeScript's narrowing is flow-based — it tracks types through loops, early returns, and assignments. When you assign x = 'hello' inside an if block, x is narrowed to string for the rest of that block. Loop narrowing: TypeScript can narrow inside for/while loops. The type of a variable can widen after a loop if the loop might not execute. Branded types: using a discriminant field on primitives: type UserId = number & { __brand: 'UserId' } — nominal typing for primitives.

questions.question: After `if (typeof x === 'string') { ... }`, what is the type of x in the else branch if x was typed as `string | number`?
options: number — TypeScript eliminates string from the union
any — TypeScript gives up narrowing in else
never — the else branch is unreachable
questions.explanation: TypeScript's control flow analysis narrows the type: in the if block, x is string. In the else block, TypeScript knows x is NOT a string (we just checked), so it eliminates string from the union. What remains is number. This is called type narrowing — TypeScript gets smarter about the type at each code location.

faq.q: What is a user-defined type guard (function x is T)?
faq.a: A function that returns `x is T` (a type predicate) as its return type. When called, TypeScript narrows x to type T in the true branch. Example: function isString(x: unknown): x is string { return typeof x === 'string' }. This lets you encapsulate a narrowing check and reuse it across your codebase.

examples: if (response instanceof Error) — distinguish errors from data
function isApiError(x: unknown): x is ApiError { return 'code' in (x as any) }
Redux reducer: switch (action.type) — each case narrows action to specific variant
